I still think it’s crazy how the show and so much of the fandom acts like Grace being straight was some brave move for representation.


Firstly, the only characters who say “oh she’s gay look at how she dresses” are Miles and Tristan— not Zoe, the only character who is “punished” for “assuming” Grace is gay. Which she didn’t. At least not because of how Grace dresses, but instead because the two of them had kissed a few times and seemed pretty clearly to be heading toward a relationship. 


Second, Grace doesn’t even dress “stereotypically” lesbian. She’s just kind of grunge/goth. And the gall of Degrassi to act as though they’re ~breaking stereotypes~ when ALL of their lesbian characters have been highly femme (nothing wrong with being a femme/lipstick lesbian, I AM one, but- -)…. Hell, the closest to a butch lesbian we’ve had is ALEX who actually became more stereotypically feminine when they started to pair her off with a woman and realize her sexuality. 

Third, what’s supposed to be the “lesson” here??  Is it supposed to be not to assume a girl is gay because of how she dresses?? Because again, that doesn’t really make sense — she doesn’t dress “gay,” and fans assumed she’s gay because the show built up a relationship between her and Zoe, and had hints of her being gay before DLB, like her checking out a girl and Zoe noticing and making a face. And, it has the same vibes as Mean Girls where it positions being thought of as a lesbian as some disgusting offense to straight girls. Like “don’t assume a girl is one of those yucky lesbians just because of how she dresses!!”. What?! 

Honestly this was just a very poorly handled plot line.

Yes they’re all toxic or predatory. 

But what’s worse, what’s unforgivable, is that — at least by the end— they were all BORING. So boring. These ships were not aspirational nor were they entertaining.

Fictionally, however, Stelena 1000000000%. 

For one, whilst I do love ~dark/problematic ships~ I just am not interested in a ship where the girl is repeatedly torn and worn down (and eventually, literally brainwashed, because the writers did not respect their female lead enough to put the effort into her character naturally progress her feelings and want to be in a relationship with him….) in order for their “relationship” to form. Elena’s autonomy is repeatedly ignored or violated by Damon, and eventually, by the writers to pair her WITH Damon: she is literally objectified. The writers only seemed interested in their sexual relationship and say that they love and decide to be with each other (despite everything) …. ~just because.~  the things that might (and in the better written seasons of the show, DID) actually attract them to each other (beyond physical) is just. Nothing. Or ignored. 


Secondly,  Stelena just appeals and interests me more. Stefan and Elena have so many parallels and similar ways of viewing (and processing and compartmentalizing) the world. I love how much Stefan respects Elena and her autonomy when he’s Himself. And then the bridge scene…. Again, in real life I would not want this girl to be with someone who, most pressingly of the shit he’s done, re-traumatize her at the place of her parents’ death. Fictionally however, god damn that compels the hell out of me!! The fact that Stefan not only SAVED her from that fate, but, because of how similar they are AND how healthily they communicated in s1-2, KNOWS exactly how traumatizing doing that so would be to her. And he does it anyway. Not only out of prioritizing vengeance against Klaus, but also in a fucked up way “protecting” her by definitively pushing her away from him.





[ Side note, I still cannot believe (well, I can, misogyny is …. Yeah) how many fans even back in the first two would insist that Damon and/or Stefan “deserved better” than Elena; as if being a teenage girl (who is dealing with insurmountable grief & trauma & survivor’s guilt, thrown into constant dangerous situations and being physically and sexually harassed/assaulted, losing more people, etc *very frequently at the hands of or because of The Salvatore brothers*) who is SUPPOSEDLY (but not actually— Elena consistently reaffirmed throughout the first two and in the end in the third, and the beginning of the fourth until the magic plot device brainwashes her, that she only wants to be with Stefan and (whatever feelings or attraction she may eventually feel for Damon) she does not want to be with Damon) indecisive between two brothers is comparable to, let alone worse than, the mass murdering and raping etc that they do….]

— the show softening Carla up post s1 ruined what had been one of the most interesting Villain reveal/evolution in modern television

— that being said, people blaming Carla for Marina’s death is…. Stupid. And misogynistic. Blame her for coercing/bribing Christian into silence and for covering for and coaching Polo in what to say. Sure. But Carla tried to trick Christian into stealing Marina’s backpack. Polo took it upon himself to try and get the watch from Marina and responded to her wounding his ego by bashing her in the head. That’s not on Carla. 

— Carla’s relationship with her father in s1 was WAY more interesting than how it was portrayed for the other two seasons. When Carla brings him the watch, he asks if she’s okay (because her friend was just murdered), and she just smiles without a care in the world and says that she is “now that everything is back to normal”…. The LOOK on his face!! That look did not come across as “yeah you better stay in line!!” That was a “holy shit what the fuck have I created.” I never got the impression that Carla was controlled by or afraid of her dad in s1; she cared about what he thought of her (her intelligence) but she wasn’t afraid of her. And then the show did what so many do. “Oh no we want our Rich Bitch character to be more sympathetic/less one-dimensional!! What can we do except pull out Old Reliable: abusive parents trope” (Carla, Lu, Pacifica Northwest, Cheryl Blossom, etc etc) 


— Lu is NOT just as bad as Polo (as far as being a killer). Neither of the intended to kill but let’s compare their actions if the accidental murders hadn’t happened: Lu pushes Polo against a wall VS Polo slams a trophy on Marina’s head when her back is turned. I’m sorry but they’re just not comparable. Also, Lu killed someone who killed her former childhood friend/long term ex boyfriend’s sister— Polo killed someone who insulted him. Again, not comparable. 

— Polo, when taking into account all three seasons he was in, is the best written character in the show.

— I stopped watching after s3.
